examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있으면 견갑골 주변이 뻐근해요.
examples.en: If I sit for a long time, the area around my shoulder blades gets stiff.
The doctor said there is a crack in my shoulder blade.

examples.ko: 이 운동은 견갑골을 모아 주는 자세가 중요해요.
examples.en: In this exercise, the posture of squeezing the shoulder blades together is important.
My shoulder blades look sticking out, and it bothers me.
Try pointing to where your shoulder blade is with your hand.
I carried a heavy bag, and even my shoulder blades hurt.

explain: 병원이나 운동 이야기에서 많이 쓰는 말이고, 쉬운 우리말로는 '날개뼈'라고 해요. 등 위쪽, 어깨 뒤에 있는 뼈를 가리켜요. '견갑골 운동'처럼 헬스 이야기에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My shoulder blade hurt, so I got a massage.
phrases.nuance_en: The plain Korean word for 견갑골.

phrases.en: My shoulder blade hurts when I drive for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 아픈 곳을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used at the hospital to say where it hurts.

phrases.en: I stretch my shoulder blades before studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동이나 건강 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in exercise and health talk.

explain_en: It is common in talk about hospitals and exercise, and the plainer Korean word is '날개뼈'. It points to the bone at the upper back behind the shoulder. It also often appears in fitness talk, as in '견갑골 운동'.

examples.ko: 선수들이 대회를 앞두고 구슬땀을 흘리며 훈련해요.
examples.en: The players train, dripping with sweat, ahead of the tournament.

examples.ko: 더운 날 이마에 구슬땀이 송골송골 맺혔어요.
examples.en: On the hot day, beads of sweat formed on my forehead.
I worked without even a moment to wipe away the sweat.
The sweat the farmers shed was not in vain.
My shirt got completely soaked with sweat.

examples.ko: 구슬땀 흘린 만큼 좋은 결과가 나올 거예요.
examples.en: You'll get good results in proportion to the sweat you put in.

explain: 구슬처럼 맺힌 굵은 땀방울인데, 보통 '구슬땀을 흘리다'로 써서 열심히 노력하는 모습을 칭찬해요. 그냥 더워서 나는 땀은 '땀'이라고 해요. 운동, 일, 훈련 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 매일 구슬땀을 흘린 덕에 시험에 합격했어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to working hard every day, I passed the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더워서 땀이 나는 것만이 아니라 힘들게 열심히 노력한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Beyond sweating from heat, it means working or training with great effort.
phrases.en_equiv: sweat it out; put in hard effort

explain_en: It refers to big sweat drops that bead up like marbles, and it is usually used as '구슬땀을 흘리다' to praise someone working hard. Plain sweat from heat is just '땀'. It often appears when talking about sports, work, and training.

examples.en: The hospital gave the patient a blood transfusion.

examples.ko: 사고로 피를 많이 흘려서 바로 수혈해야 해요.
examples.en: A lot of blood was lost in the accident, so a transfusion must be given right away.
Before giving a transfusion, they check the blood type.
The doctor is getting ready to give a transfusion.
I heard they gave a transfusion during yesterday's surgery.
After a blood transfusion, the body gets much better.

explain: '수혈하다'는 '환자에게 수혈하다'처럼 피를 넣어 주는 쪽에서 써요. 받는 사람 입장에서는 '수혈을 받다'라고 해요. 피를 내주는 일은 '헌혈하다'예요.

phrases.en: The injured person received a blood transfusion at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피를 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person receiving blood.

phrases.en: The doctor gave the patient a blood transfusion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자에게 피를 넣어 주는 의사나 간호사 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the one who gives the transfusion, such as a doctor or nurse.

phrases.example: 수술 중에 수혈이 필요할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: A blood transfusion may be needed during surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피가 모자라서 넣어야 할 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when blood is lacking and must be given.

explain_en: '수혈하다' is used from the side giving blood to the patient, as in '환자에게 수혈하다'. From the patient's side, you say '수혈을 받다'. Donating blood is '헌혈하다'.

examples.en: I wrapped my knee, which I hurt in a fall, with a bandage.

examples.ko: 추워서 목도리로 얼굴을 꽁꽁 싸매고 나갔어요.
examples.en: It was cold, so I went out with my face wrapped up tightly in a scarf.
His finger was cut, so I wrapped it up with a handkerchief for him.

examples.ko: 상처를 싸매기 전에 먼저 깨끗이 씻으세요.
examples.en: Wash the wound clean before you bandage it.
She wrapped the baby in a blanket and carried him.
He came to school with his leg bandaged up.

explain: 다친 곳이나 몸의 일부를 천이나 붕대로 감싸서 묶는다는 느낌이에요. '감다'보다 전체를 덮어 싼다는 느낌이 강해요. '머리를 싸매다'는 관용적으로도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 시험 문제 때문에 모두 머리를 싸매고 고민했어요.
phrases.en: Everyone racked their brains over the exam question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 머리를 감싸는 게 아니라, 어려운 일을 해결하려고 온 힘을 다해 생각하거나 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It doesn't mean wrapping your head; it means thinking or studying with all your effort to solve something hard.

explain_en: It means covering and tying up an injured spot or body part with cloth or a bandage. It feels more like wrapping the whole thing than '감다' (to wind around). '머리를 싸매다' is also a very common idiom.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 독감 백신을 접종해요.
examples.en: I get a flu shot before winter comes.
I got the child the necessary vaccines on time.

examples.ko: 백신을 접종하고 나서 하루 정도 쉬었어요.
examples.en: After getting the vaccine, I rested for about a day.

examples.ko: 접종하기 전에 의사 선생님께 몸 상태를 말해야 해요.
examples.en: Before vaccination, you need to tell the doctor how you feel.
I heard the school is vaccinating students in groups.

examples.ko: 접종한 팔이 조금 아파서 무거운 걸 못 들어요.
examples.en: The arm I got the shot in is a bit sore, so I can't lift heavy things.

explain: 접종하다는 몸에 백신을 넣어서 병을 예방한다는 말이에요. 맞는 사람 쪽에서는 '접종을 받다', '백신을 맞다', '주사 맞다'라고 해요. 의사나 병원 쪽에서는 '접종하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I got vaccinated at the hospital yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞는 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person receiving the shot.

phrases.en: I'm getting a flu vaccine tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 쉽고 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easiest and most natural phrase in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 접종 후에는 열이 날 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You may get a fever after vaccination.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '접종' to talk about timing.

explain_en: It means putting a vaccine into the body to prevent disease. The person receiving it says '접종을 받다', '백신을 맞다' or '주사 맞다'. The doctor's or hospital's side uses 접종하다.

examples.en: Time heals the wounds of the heart.
This music heals tired people.
That book healed my heart.

examples.ko: 아픈 마음을 치유하는 데는 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: Healing a hurt heart takes time.

examples.ko: 산책을 하면서 스스로를 치유할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I was able to heal myself while taking walks.
We created this program to help heal the children.

explain: '치유하다'는 몸의 병뿐 아니라 마음의 상처에도 많이 써요. 병원에서 병을 고칠 때는 '치료하다'가 일반적이에요. '고치다'도 쓰지만 물건이나 습관에 더 어울려요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 상처와 함께 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used with emotional wounds.
치료하다 is the usual word for medical treatment.

phrases.en: Right now I need time to heal.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 치유 as a noun for a period of recovery.

explain_en: 치유하다 is used for emotional wounds as much as for bodily illness. For a hospital treating a disease, 치료하다 is the usual word. 고치다 also works, but it fits objects and habits better.

dis.h: heal, especially wounds of the heart

p.n: 치료하다 is clinical and does not fit emotional wounds well.
